props.title: Our process
props.description: How the Global Canopy Atlas is built — from raw airborne LiDAR to an open, standardised global canopy dataset.

props.heading: 01_Raw data ingestion & discovery
props.body: We gathered disparate airborne LiDAR data from thousands of unique flights worldwide, covering everything from dense tropical rainforests to sparse boreal woodlands.

props.heading: 02_Data harmonisation & quality control
props.body: Raw point clouds were put through a uniform quality-control workflow to remove errors, normalize terrain variations, and resolve flight-line overlaps, ensuring cross-biome consistency.

props.heading: 03_Open access distribution
props.body: The Global Canopy Atlas is built entirely on the principles of open science and public accessibility, with 87% of the atlas data entirely open-access under a CC-BY 4.0 international license.

props.heading: Delivering an interactive map of global canopy
props.body: By processing and harmonising 3,458 airborne laser scanning (ALS) acquisitions, we have created a uniform, open-access dataset covering 56,554 km² across the world's major biomes.

props.heading: What makes it all possible
props.subheading: This project is the result of an unprecedented global collaboration between international research labs, space agencies, and field ecologists. By pooling resources and standardizing independent datasets, we've built a shared foundation for the future of forest conservation.

items.question: What source data does the atlas use?
items.answer: Airborne laser scanning (ALS) acquisitions contributed by more than 100 institutions, harmonised into a single open dataset.

items.question: What licence is the data released under?
items.answer: The majority of the atlas (87%) is released open-access under a CC-BY 4.0 international license.

items.question: How is quality controlled?
items.answer: Every point cloud passes a uniform QC workflow that removes errors, normalises terrain, and resolves flight-line overlaps.

items.question: Can I contribute data?
items.answer: Yes — we are always looking for new collaborators and data contributors. Get in touch via the contact page.
